newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil inactive, diesel cargoes steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil inactive, diesel cargoes steady.

text.p: European physical gas oil eased in line with weaker futures on Friday but most differentials were assessed at steady numbers in very slow talk, traders said.
A flexi cargo of low sulphur diesel traded at a steady differential of $5.25 over September IPE cif Le Havre for the second half of August, they said.
It was the only physical trade completed in a quiet market stalled by the Ascension Day holiday in much of the continent.
September IPE settled down $2.50 to $171.50 a tonne, following easier Brent and catching up with crude's late losses on Thursday. October closed at $173.00, also down $2.50.
Heating oil was discussed sporadically but no firm agreement to exchange product was heard. German DIN quality was assessed at premiums of around 75 cents bid and $1.25 offered.
"There does seem to be a certain amount of buying -- the contango is almost as good as it is going to get," another trader said. "But not much looks like getting done."

Rotterdam refinery barges were hardly discussed at all in a very slack afternoon. Levels were notionally at September IPE -$0.50/$0.00, around unchanged. Low sulphur diesel remained notionally at around $4 over the September screen.
